s: Which commission on Centre-State relations was constituted by the Union Government in June 1983 under a retired Supreme Court judge?
x: The Sarkaria Commission was set up by the Centre in June 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria, a retired Supreme Court judge, and reported in 1988 with 247 recommendations. The Rajamannar Committee (1969) was appointed by Tamil Nadu, the ARC dates to 1966, and the Punchhi Commission came later (2007).

s: Who headed the study team on Centre-State relations of the Administrative Reforms Commission (1966)?
x: M.C. Setalvad headed the study team; the ARC itself was chaired first by Morarji Desai and later by K. Hanumanthaiya.

s: Which one of the following is the odd one out among bodies associated with reviewing Centre-State relations?
x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with State funding of elections (partial funding in kind to recognised parties), not Centre-State relations. The Rajamannar Committee (1969), the Sarkaria Commission (1983) and the ARC (1966, Setalvad study team) all reviewed Centre-State relations.

s: Who chaired the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (2000)?
x: The NCRWC was chaired by former CJI M.N. Venkatachaliah; Punchhi headed the 2007 commission.

s: In which year was the Punchhi Commission on Centre-State relations appointed by the Centre?
x: The Punchhi Commission was appointed on 27 April 2007 and reported on 30 March 2010.

s: Who was the first chairman of the Administrative Reforms Commission set up in 1966?
x: The ARC (1966) was first chaired by Morarji Desai, later by K. Hanumanthaiya; M.C. Setalvad headed its study team on Centre-State relations.

s: How many recommendations did the Punchhi Commission on Centre-State relations make?
x: The Punchhi Commission (2007, report 2010) made 273 recommendations; Sarkaria made 247.

s: In which year did the Punchhi Commission submit its report?
x: The Punchhi Commission was appointed on 27 April 2007 and reported on 30 March 2010.

s: Under which Prime Minister's government was the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution set up in February 2000?
x: The NCRWC under M.N. Venkatachaliah was set up by the Vajpayee government on 22 February 2000 and reported in 2002.

s: Which one of the following was a recommendation of the Rajamannar Committee?
o: Appointment of Governors as recent active politicians
A four-month period for assent to every Bill
Strengthening of the All India Services
x: The Rajamannar Committee recommended abolishing the Planning Commission, eliminating Article 356 and establishing an Inter-State Council under Article 263.

s: What did the Sarkaria Commission propose on residuary powers?
o: all residuary powers go to the States
residuary taxation stay with Parliament and other residuary matters go to the Concurrent List
all residuary powers, including taxation, go to the Concurrent List
all residuary powers remain exclusively with Parliament
x: Sarkaria proposed keeping residuary taxation with Parliament and placing the remaining residuary matters in the Concurrent List.

s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission?
o: Abolition of the All India Services
Use of Article 356 very sparingly and as a last resort
Consultation with States on laws relating to the Concurrent List
x: The Sarkaria Commission favoured strengthening the All India Services, not abolishing them.

s: Which of the following was recommended by the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution regarding the Governor's handling of Bills?
o: The Governor should decide Bills only after a referendum
Every Bill should be reserved for the President
Assent should be withheld indefinitely in case of disagreement with the State Cabinet
Assent should be given within about four months
x: The NCRWC recommended that assent to Bills should be given within about four months. It also suggested safeguards concerning Article 356 and an order of preference in a hung Assembly.

s: Which body proposed the concept of a 'localised emergency'?
x: The Punchhi Commission proposed the localised emergency; Rajamannar sought deletion of Article 356 and Sarkaria treated it as a last resort.

s: Which commission recommended that Governors be removed only through a procedure similar to the impeachment of the President?
x: The Punchhi Commission recommended a fixed tenure for Governors and a President-like (impeachment) removal procedure (APPSC-G1 2024 key), along with time-bound disposal of Bills and the localised emergency idea. Sarkaria wanted an eminent outsider as Governor, Rajamannar sought deletion of Article 356, and the ARC urged non-partisan Governors.

s: The complete deletion of Article 356 was demanded by the:
x: Deleting Article 356 was the Rajamannar Committee's demand; the ARC recommended an Inter-State Council and non-partisan Governors.

s: Which body recommended that the Governor give assent to Bills within about four months?
o: National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution
x: The NCRWC recommended assent within about four months.

s: In which period did the coalition era, giving the States a greater say in Centre-State relations, begin?
x: Congress dominance marked the 1950s and early 1960s, opposition State governments rose from the mid-1960s, and the coalition era began in the 1990s.

s: Which body replaced the Planning Commission in 2015?
x: The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

s: With which of the following propositions is the decision in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) associated?
o: The Governor has unlimited discretion in all matters
Article 356 action is completely beyond judicial scrutiny
The GST Council has binding legislative authority
Article 356 action is subject to judicial review
x: S.R. Bommai established that the exercise of power under Article 356 is reviewable by the courts.

s: As what was the Planning Commission criticised in the federal context?
o: a statutory body collecting taxes on behalf of States
a judicial body adjudicating disputes between States
an extra-constitutional body that made States dependent on the Union for aid
a constitutional body controlling State Legislatures
x: Critics called the Planning Commission an extra-constitutional institution that made States 'suppliants for aid'.

s: Along with Articles 256, 257 and 365, which Article is criticised in federalism debates as an instrument of Union overreach?
x: Articles 356, 256, 257 and 365 are identified as provisions that may enable excessive Union intervention.

s: Cesses are criticised in federalism debates mainly because they:
o: Are not shared with the States
Are levied only by the States
Are fixed by the Finance Commission
x: Cesses (about 18% of gross tax revenue) are not shared with the States.

s:
Consider the following:
1. Office of the Governor
2. All India Services
3. Planning Commission
4. Inter-State Council
Which of the above have been criticised as being against the federal principle?
x: The Governor, All India Services and Planning Commission are criticised as tools of central control; the Inter-State Council is a forum for cooperation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about All India Services and State autonomy?
o: All India Services have no role in Centre-State coordination
Officers are governed in important respects by Central rules
States cannot fully discipline or remove such officers
Officers are recruited by the UPSC but serve in the States
x: All India Services are also defended as promoting Centre-State coordination.

s: In which body must a resolution supported by two-thirds of members present and voting be passed to create a new All India Service?
x: The resolution must be passed by the Rajya Sabha, not the Lok Sabha.

s: How is control over All India Services officers divided?
o: Ultimate and immediate control both with the Centre
Ultimate control with the Centre, immediate with the States
Ultimate control with the States, immediate with the Centre
x: AIS officers are under the ultimate control of the Centre and the immediate control of the States.

s: Article 312 deals with the All India Services, which include IAS, IPS and which other service?
x: Under Article 312 the All India Services are the IAS, IPS and Indian Forest Service.

s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The All India Services are criticised as violating the federal principle.
Reason (R): Their officers serve the States, but ultimate control over them lies with the Centre.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: AIS officers serve States but are under ultimate central control, which is why they are said to violate the federal principle.

s: The defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill, 2026 on Lok Sabha expansion sharpened which debate?
o: The debate on abolishing local governments
x: The defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill on Lok Sabha expansion sharpened the North–South debate.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 371E – Central University in Andhra Pradesh
Article 371D – Central University in Andhra Pradesh
x: Article 371E concerns a Central University in Andhra Pradesh; 371A is Nagaland, 371D local cadres, education and jobs in AP, and 371F Sikkim.

s: Which body granted Special Category Status, which is not provided for in the Constitution, to States?
x: SCS was granted by the National Development Council using the Gadgil formula criteria.

s: What did the Union Government provide to Andhra Pradesh instead of granting the promised Special Category Status?
o: A separate Finance Commission for Andhra Pradesh
x: The Centre subsequently provided a special assistance package in 2016 instead of granting SCS.

s: What was the Central share in funding of plan spending under Special Category Status?
x: SCS involved 90 per cent Central funding of plan spending; the 14th Finance Commission instead raised devolution to 42 per cent and used revenue deficit grants.

s: The stand of which Finance Commission was the Centre's main reason for denying Special Category Status?
x: The 14th FC raised devolution to 42% and drew no distinction between special and general category States.

s: Which Article provides for local cadres, education and jobs in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Article 371D covers AP's local cadres, education and jobs; 371E provides for a Central University in AP.

s: How many States were granted Special Category Status?
x: Eleven States were granted SCS, e.g. Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh and J&K; Bihar never was.

s: What are the Special Category Status criteria applied by the NDC known as?
x: The NDC granted SCS using Gadgil formula criteria such as hilly terrain, border location and backwardness.

s: To what share did the 14th Finance Commission raise the States' share in the divisible pool of central taxes?
x: The 14th Finance Commission raised devolution to 42% and made no distinction between special and general category States.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Article)          List-II (State)
A. Article 371A           1. Assam
B. Article 371B           2. Manipur
C. Article 371C           3. Nagaland
D. Article 371            4. Maharashtra and Gujarat
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Art. 371 – Maharashtra and Gujarat; 371A – Nagaland; 371B – Assam; 371C – Manipur.

s: Over how many subjects does the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority (2026) give eastern Nagaland autonomy?
x: The FNTA gives eastern Nagaland autonomy over 46 subjects without affecting Article 371A.

s: Ladakh was offered Article 371 safeguards (2026) instead of which constitutional provision it had demanded?
x: Ladakh was offered Article 371-type safeguards instead of inclusion in the Sixth Schedule.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State autonomy debate in India?
o: Autonomy demands grew after the Congress lost power in many States in the mid-1960s
Coalition politics after the 1990s led towards more cooperative federalism
The Punjab militancy of the 1980s is cited in favour of greater State autonomy
The Punjab militancy of the 1980s is cited to stress national unity
x: The Punjab militancy is cited against greater autonomy, stressing unity.

s: With which States was the demand to restrict the Centre to defence, foreign affairs, currency and communications associated?
x: This four-subject demand is associated with Punjab and West Bengal; Tamil Nadu's position sought deletion of Article 356 and abolition of the All India Services and Planning Commission.

s: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution, a State autonomy demand, is associated with which State?
x: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution came from Punjab; the Rajamannar Committee belongs to Tamil Nadu.

s: What have State autonomy demands in India mainly sought?
o: more powers, greater own revenue and less central administrative control
transfer of defence and foreign affairs to local bodies
a uniform language policy for all States
abolition of State legislatures and central taxation
x: Autonomy demands sought more powers for States, more control over own revenue and reduced central administrative control.

s: In which year did West Bengal's Left Front government present the CPI(M) memorandum on State autonomy?
x: West Bengal's CPI(M) memorandum came in 1977, after Tamil Nadu (1969) and Punjab (1973).

s: Which was cited as an argument against greater State autonomy, in the interest of national unity?
x: Punjab militancy of the 1980s is cited against greater autonomy on grounds of unity.

s: A principal argument for greater State autonomy is that States:
o: have surplus revenue beyond their needs
lack adequate resources for the duties assigned to them
have no role in delivering public services
x: A major argument for State autonomy is that States often lack sufficient resources to perform their constitutionally assigned duties.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about central agencies and State consent?
o: The Enforcement Directorate needs a State's general consent to enforce PMLA and FEMA there
The NIA can investigate scheduled offences without State consent
The NIA functions under the NIA Act, 2008
Under Section 6 of the DSPE Act, 1946, the CBI needs State consent to act in a State
x: The ED enforces PMLA, 2002 and FEMA, 1999 nationwide with no State consent needed.

s: What happens if a State withdraws general consent to the CBI?
o: its cases pass automatically to the NIA
the CBI must obtain consent case by case
the CBI is permanently barred from all cases in the State
the CBI may investigate on Union direction without approval
x: Withdrawal of general consent means the CBI must seek the State's consent separately for each case.

s: Which of the following central agencies needs State consent to investigate in a State?
x: Only the CBI needs State consent, under Section 6 of the DSPE Act, 1946; the NIA and ED do not.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The CBI works under the DSPE Act, 1946; the ED under PMLA 2002 and FEMA 1999; the NIA under the NIA Act, 2008.

s: Which State challenged the NIA Act, 2008 in the Supreme Court in January 2020?
x: Chhattisgarh challenged the NIA Act in the Supreme Court in January 2020 as intruding on the States' police power.

s: After which event was the NIA Act, 2008 enacted?
x: The National Investigation Agency Act was passed in 2008 after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks.

s: Which of the following States had withdrawn general consent to the CBI, according to a Lok Sabha reply of December 2023?
x: The Dec 2023 Lok Sabha list of States that withdrew general consent included Telangana, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Punjab and others; Gujarat, Odisha and AP were not on it.

s: Which one of the following explains fiscal centralisation after GST?
o: GST abolished the divisible pool of Union taxes.
State taxes expanded and all cesses entered the divisible pool.
Cesses and surcharges automatically joined the divisible pool.
GST subsumed several State taxes, while cesses and surcharges stayed outside the divisible pool.
x: GST subsumed several State taxes, while cesses and surcharges remain outside the divisible pool.

s: Which of the following strengthens local fiscal devolution rather than being cited in the centralisation critique?
x: State Finance Commissions strengthen local fiscal devolution; cesses, CSS and GST are cited as centralising.

s: What is the vote weight of the Centre in the GST Council?
x: The Centre has one-third of the weighted vote and the States two-thirds; decisions need a three-fourths majority.

s: In Mohit Minerals (May 2022), what did the Supreme Court hold about GST Council recommendations?
o: Binding on both Union and States
x: Mohit Minerals held that GST Council recommendations are not binding on the Union and States; they have persuasive value.

s: What share of the divisible pool has the 16th Finance Commission recommended for States for 2026-31?
x: The 16th FC keeps 41%; States wanted 50%, while the 14th FC had given 42%.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the GST Council?
x: The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Amendment.

s: What majority of the weighted votes is needed for a decision of the GST Council?
x: The Centre has one-third and the States two-thirds of the vote weight; decisions need a three-fourths majority of weighted votes.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in its opinion of 20 November 2025 on a Presidential Reference?
o: Courts can fix timelines for the Governor's assent
No court-imposed timelines apply to the Governor or President
Deemed assent is part of the Constitution
The Governor must assent within four months
x: The 5-judge bench held there are no court-imposed timelines under Articles 200 and 201, and deemed assent is alien to the Constitution.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Governor-State conflicts?
o: Bill assent delays arose in Tamil Nadu and Kerala
In State of Tamil Nadu v Governor (April 2025), the SC set timelines for assent
The Presidential Reference was made under Article 143
x: The November 2025 opinion called deemed assent alien to the Constitution; the other statements are correct.

s: Who set up the Kurian Joseph Committee, which seeks a 'structural reset' of federal relations?
x: The Kurian Joseph Committee was appointed by Tamil Nadu; Part I came on 16 February 2026.

s: Who chairs the Inter-State Council set up in 1990 under Article 263?
x: The Prime Minister chairs the Inter-State Council; the Home Minister chairs its Standing Committee.

s: When was the 11th and last meeting of the Inter-State Council held?
x: The Inter-State Council's 11th meeting, the last, was held on 16 July 2016.

s: How many Union Cabinet ministers are members of the Inter-State Council?
x: Members include CMs, UT administrators, Governors of States under President's Rule and six Union Cabinet ministers.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Rajamannar Committee:
1. It found that central dominance had turned the States into 'administrative units of the Centre'.
2. It identified Articles 280 and 282 as the main instruments of this overreach.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct; the Articles it named as enabling overreach were 256, 257 and 365, not 280 and 282.

s: Under which Article did the Rajamannar Committee recommend the immediate setting up of a permanent Inter-State Council?
x: Rajamannar wanted a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263 at once, along with a revitalised Finance Commission.

s: What did the Rajamannar Committee recommend with reference to Article 356?
o: Its complete deletion from the Constitution
Its wider application during constitutional emergencies
Its transfer from the Constitution to ordinary law
Its use only with the approval of the Inter-State Council
x: The committee recommended the complete elimination of Article 356 as part of reducing central control over the States.

s: The Rajamannar Committee viewed the Planning Commission as an extra-constitutional body because it:
o: controlled the recruitment to All-India Services
appointed the Governors of the States
alone decided grants to the States
x: The committee criticised the Planning Commission as an extra-constitutional body that alone decided grants to the States and recommended its abolition.

s: For what main purpose did the Rajamannar Committee recommend abolition of the All-India Services?
o: Reduce central administrative control over State governments
Transfer recruitment to the Planning Commission
Create a separate service for each district
Increase the control of the Union over State governments
x: Abolition of the All-India Services was recommended to reduce central administrative control over State governments.

s: What did the Rajamannar Committee recommend on the Finance Commission?
x: Rajamannar wanted the Finance Commission revitalised and revenue devolution widened.

s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Rajamannar Committee?
x: Rajamannar did not recommend strengthening the Governor (APPSC-G2 2017); the others were its recommendations.

s: Which one of the following was NOT among the examples of subjects proposed for transfer to the State List?
x: Inland waterway navigation, industrial disputes, and oil fields regulation and development were cited examples. Foreign affairs was not among them.

s: On residuary powers, what did the Rajamannar Committee and the Sarkaria Commission respectively favour?
o: the States; the Concurrent List for non-tax residuary matters
x: Rajamannar wanted residuary powers given to the States; Sarkaria placed residuary powers other than taxation in the Concurrent List.

s: With which of the following did the Rajamannar Committee recommend that residuary powers be vested?
x: Rajamannar wanted residuary powers given to the States; Sarkaria put non-tax residuary matters in the Concurrent List.

s: Who constituted the Rajamannar Committee (1969) on Centre-State relations?
x: The Tamil Nadu Government set up the Rajamannar Committee in 1969; its recommendations were never implemented by the Centre.

s: In which year was the Rajamannar Committee constituted?
x: The Rajamannar Committee was constituted in 1969, before Sarkaria (1983), NCRWC (2000) and Punchhi (2007).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: P.V. Rajamannar – former Chief Justice, Bombay High Court
P.V. Rajamannar – former Chief Justice, Madras High Court
x: P.V. Rajamannar was a former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court; the committee was appointed in 1969 and reported in 1971.

s: The Rajamannar Committee is significant as which of the following?
o: first Union-appointed commission on Centre-State relations
first committee on Centre-State relations appointed by a State
first committee to recommend abolishing the Finance Commission
first committee formed after the Inter-State Council was set up
x: The Rajamannar Committee was the first committee on Centre-State relations appointed by a State.

s: Besides the Rajamannar Committee, which Finance Commission did P.V. Rajamannar chair?
x: P.V. Rajamannar chaired both the Rajamannar Committee and the Fourth Finance Commission.

s: Which Chief Minister headed the Tamil Nadu DMK government that appointed the Rajamannar Committee?
x: The DMK government under Karunanidhi appointed it in 1969, taking forward Annadurai's 1967 view.

s: Besides its Chairman and A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar, who was a member of the Rajamannar Committee?
x: A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar and P. Chandra Reddy were the other two members; R.S. Sarkaria chaired a later commission.

s: What was the formal name of the Rajamannar Committee appointed by Tamil Nadu in 1969?
x: The Rajamannar Committee was formally the Centre-State Relations Inquiry Committee.

s: Whose 1967 view, that the Union need not control health and education, did the Rajamannar Committee take forward?
x: The Rajamannar Committee took forward C.N. Annadurai's 1967 view that the Union need not control health and education.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rajamannar Committee?
o: It was to identify the causes of unitary tendencies in the working of the Constitution
It was to suggest measures securing the utmost autonomy for the States
It was to strengthen the Centre's control over education and health
x: The committee sought to reduce central control, including over subjects such as education and health.

s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended ending central control over which pair of subjects?
x: The committee sought to end central control over education and health and to move more Concurrent subjects to the State List.

s: What was the immediate response of the Union Government to the Rajamannar Committee report?
o: It ignored the report and took no action on it.
It accepted the recommendations on Article 356 but rejected all others.
It referred the report to the Finance Commission for implementation.
It implemented all its recommendations through a constitutional amendment.
x: The Centre ignored the report and took no action on its recommendations.

s: Through the influence of which body was the Inter-State Council established in 1990?
x: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 through the Sarkaria Commission's influence.

s: When did the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly adopt a State autonomy resolution on the basis of the Rajamannar report?
x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly adopted the State autonomy resolution in April 1974 on the basis of the report.

s: In which year was the Kurian Joseph Committee on Centre-State relations appointed?
x: The Kurian Joseph Committee was appointed in April 2025, after Rajamannar (1969), Sarkaria (1983) and Punchhi (2007).

s: What was the DMK slogan linked to the Rajamannar report?
o: Autonomy for the States, federalism at the Centre
x: The DMK slogan was 'autonomy for the States, federalism at the Centre'.

s:
Consider the following statements about the aftermath of the Rajamannar report:
1. The Tamil Nadu Assembly adopted a State autonomy resolution in April 1974.
2. The Inter-State Council of 1990 was set up on its recommendation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The TN resolution came in April 1974; the ISC (1990) came through Sarkaria, not Rajamannar.

s: In which year did the Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations submit its report?
x: The Sarkaria Commission was set up in June 1983 and submitted its report in 1988.

s: In which year was the Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations set up?
x: The Sarkaria Commission was set up in June 1983 and submitted its report in 1988.

s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the Sarkaria Commission?
x: The Sarkaria Commission had R.S. Sarkaria, B. Sivaraman and S.R. Sen; M.M. Punchhi headed a later commission set up in 2007.

s: Justice R.S. Sarkaria, who chaired the Commission on Centre-State relations, was a retired judge of which court?
x: Justice Rajinder Singh Sarkaria was a retired Supreme Court judge; his report made 247 recommendations.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Sarkaria Commission:
1. It was to suggest changes in Centre-State relations within the existing constitutional framework.
2. It submitted its report in 1988.
3. It was appointed by the Government of Tamil Nadu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Central Government, not Tamil Nadu, set up the Commission in June 1983.

s: Who among the following were members of the Sarkaria Commission besides its Chairman?
o: A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar and P. Chandra Reddy
x: The three-member Sarkaria Commission had Justice R.S. Sarkaria as Chairman and B. Sivaraman and Dr S.R. Sen as members.

s: How many recommendations did the Sarkaria Commission make in its report of 1988?
x: The Sarkaria Commission's report (January 1988) made 247 recommendations, of which 180 were accepted or implemented.

s: What did the Sarkaria Commission recommend on the tenure of a Governor?
o: A six-year term co-terminus with the Legislative Assembly
A secure five-year term, cut short only for extremely compelling reasons
A tenure determined exclusively by the Chief Minister
A fixed three-year term, extendable without limitation
x: The Commission recommended a secure five-year tenure, which should not be cut short except for extremely compelling reasons.

s: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that a Governor should decide on Bills:
x: Sarkaria recommended strictly non-partisan appointment of Governors and decision on Bills within a specified period.

s: Who among the following should be appointed Governor according to the Sarkaria Commission?
o: Closely involved in the local politics of the State
An eminent person from outside the State
An active politician in the recent past
Appointed without consulting the Chief Minister
x: Sarkaria favoured an eminent person from outside the State, not recently active in politics, with the Chief Minister consulted.

s: Which of the following was NOT a Sarkaria recommendation on the Governor?
o: Chief Minister to be effectively consulted
Should have travelled extensively in the State
x: 'Travelled extensively in the State' was not a criterion (APPSC-G2 2017); the others were recommended.

s: Which of the following was NOT a Sarkaria Commission recommendation on Article 356?
o: It should be used very sparingly, as a last resort
Loss of majority should be decided by the Governor's own assessment rather than a floor test
The State should be given a warning before it is invoked
Majority should be tested on the floor of the Assembly
x: Sarkaria wanted the majority tested by a floor test in the Assembly, not by the Governor's own assessment.

s: Besides S.R. Bommai (1994), in which case did the courts rely on the Sarkaria report?
x: Bommai and Rameshwar Prasad relied on Sarkaria; Kesavananda Bharati came a decade before the Commission.

s: What did the Sarkaria Commission recommend when there is doubt over a Ministry's majority?
o: A floor test in the Assembly
x: Sarkaria wanted majority tested on the floor of the Assembly, not by the Governor's own view.

s: In the case of a hung Assembly, what did the Sarkaria Commission recommend to the Governor?
o: Invite parties in a set order of preference
Call fresh elections without inviting any party
x: For a hung Assembly, Sarkaria said the Governor should invite parties in a set order of preference; Punchhi later endorsed this.

s: The Inter-State Council of 1990 implemented which Sarkaria recommendation?
o: A permanent intergovernmental forum under Article 263
Transfer of residuary taxation to the States
Mandatory dissolution of Assemblies under Article 356
x: The Inter-State Council, set up in 1990 under Article 263, is regarded as the main implemented Sarkaria recommendation.

s: What was the Sarkaria Commission's proposed name for the permanent Inter-State Council?
x: Sarkaria proposed a permanent council under Article 263 named the Inter-Governmental Council.

s: When was the Inter-State Council set up on Sarkaria's recommendation?
x: The Inter-State Council was set up on 28 May 1990; its Secretariat followed in 1991.

s: What did the Sarkaria Commission recommend the Union should do before Parliament legislates on a subject in the Concurrent List?
o: Consult the States through an institutionalised process
Seek permission from the Supreme Court
Obtain approval from every State Legislature
Refer the matter exclusively to the Finance Commission
x: The Centre should consult the States before legislating on a Concurrent List subject, preferably through an institutionalised process of prior consultation.

s: With reference to residuary powers (Article 248), the Sarkaria Commission recommended that the residuary power of taxation should:
o: be placed in the Concurrent List
be shared equally through the Finance Commission
x: Sarkaria wanted the residuary power of taxation to remain with Parliament; only residuary powers other than taxation were to go to the Concurrent List. Transfer to the States was Rajamannar's view, and equal sharing through the Finance Commission was never proposed.

s: What did the Sarkaria and Rajamannar bodies respectively recommend on All-India Services?
o: transferring them to local governments; abolishing them
x: Sarkaria wanted All-India Services strengthened and more of them created, whereas Rajamannar wanted them abolished.

s: According to the Sarkaria Commission, when may the Centre deploy central armed forces in a State?
o: Only after a Rajya Sabha resolution
x: The Centre may deploy central forces even without a request, though consulting the State first is desirable.

s: What did the Sarkaria Commission recommend on cesses and surcharges?
o: They should be collected exclusively by State governments.
They should be abolished immediately in all circumstances.
They should be kept to a minimum and be time-bound, after which they should merge into the shareable tax pool.
They should be unlimited and permanently excluded from the divisible pool.
x: The Commission recommended that cesses and surcharges be kept to a minimum and made time-bound, with their subsequent merger into the shareable tax pool.

s: What new name did the Sarkaria Commission recommend for the National Development Council?
x: Sarkaria proposed renaming the NDC as the National Economic and Development Council.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Sarkaria Commission's financial recommendations:
1. The present division of functions between the Finance Commission and the Planning Commission was found reasonable.
2. The Planning Commission should be abolished.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Sarkaria found the present division of functions reasonable and wanted it to continue; Rajamannar wanted the Planning Commission abolished.

s: Of the Sarkaria Commission's 247 recommendations, how many were accepted or implemented (2013)?
x: Per a 2013 Lok Sabha reply, 180 were accepted/implemented, 65 not accepted and 2 under implementation.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Punchhi – localised emergency and fixed tenure for Governors
Punchhi – opposition to fixed tenure for Governors
x: Punchhi proposed localised emergency and fixed tenure for Governors; Sarkaria strengthened All-India Services and Rajamannar sought State autonomy.

s: Which commission on Centre-State relations recommended a 'localised emergency' and fixed tenure for Governors?
x: The Punchhi Commission (Centre, 2007) proposed a localised emergency and fixed Governor tenure.

s: How was the agenda of the Inter-State Council to be set under the Punchhi recommendations?
o: By the Union Home Ministry alone
x: Punchhi wanted the Inter-State Council to be a working forum whose agenda is set in consultation with the States.

s: The Punchhi Commission recommended that the National Integration Council should meet at least how often?
x: Punchhi wanted the National Integration Council to meet at least once a year; thrice a year was for the Inter-State Council.

s: According to the Punchhi Commission, how often should the Inter-State Council meet?
x: Punchhi recommended that the Inter-State Council meet at least thrice a year.

s: Before Parliament legislates on a subject in the Concurrent List, what did the Punchhi Commission recommend that the Union should do?
o: refer the matter exclusively to the Finance Commission
consult only the Governor of each State
obtain approval from every State Legislature as a constitutional prerequisite
reach broad agreement with the States through the Inter-State Council
x: The Commission recommended that the Centre should reach broad agreement with the States through the Inter-State Council before legislating on Concurrent List subjects.

s: Which of the following was recommended as a new entry in the Union List?
x: The Commission recommended adding a specific Union List entry on environment, ecology and climate change.

s:
Consider the following statements about Article 249:
1. A Rajya Sabha resolution under it must be supported by two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. Such a resolution remains in force for not more than one year at a time.
3. After the 101st Amendment, it also covers the goods and services tax under Article 246A.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Article 249 needs a two-thirds Rajya Sabha resolution, lasts up to one year (renewable), and since the 101st Amendment covers GST under Article 246A.

s: What did the Punchhi Commission recommend on the role of Governors in State universities?
o: be Chancellors only during President's Rule
not be made Chancellors or given other statutory university roles
compulsorily remain Chancellors of all State universities
x: To avoid clashes with State Governments, Punchhi recommended that Governors not be made Chancellors or given statutory university roles.

s: The Punchhi Commission recommended a constitutional amendment giving the Governor how long to decide on Bills passed by the State Assembly?
x: Punchhi proposed a constitutional amendment prescribing a six-month period for the Governor to decide on Bills.

s: Which of the following Punchhi Commission recommendations on the Governor is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 156 – delete 'during the pleasure of the President'
Removal – impeachment by the State Legislature
Model for removal – impeachment of the President
Transfer – periodic rotation of Governors among States
x: Punchhi wanted the pleasure clause removed and impeachment-style removal like the President's; periodic rotation of Governors was not its recommendation.

s: Which of the following was NOT a Punchhi Commission recommendation on the Governor?
o: A fixed tenure of five years
Removal by impeachment by the State Legislature
Governors should not be Chancellors of State universities
Abolition of the office of Governor
x: Punchhi did not recommend abolishing the office of Governor; the other three were its recommendations.

s: The Punchhi Commission wanted the Governor to be an eminent person who had not been in active politics, even at the local level, for:
o: A couple of years before appointment
Five years after the end of tenure
x: It recommended an eminent person not in active politics, even locally, for a couple of years before appointment.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Punchhi Commission's recommendations on the Governor:
1. The Governor should have a fixed tenure of five years.
2. The Governor should be removed only by impeachment by the State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Punchhi wanted a fixed five-year tenure and removal only by impeachment by the State Legislature, like the President's impeachment.

s: Which Article of the Constitution did the Punchhi Commission want amended to delete the words 'during the pleasure of the President'?
x: Article 156 says the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President; Punchhi wanted these words deleted.

s: According to the Punchhi Commission, from where should the Governor of a State be appointed?
o: From among the members of the State Legislature
From among the members of the Rajya Sabha
x: Punchhi endorsed the Sarkaria norm that the Governor should be from outside the State, with the CM consulted.

s: Who served as the Chairman of the Commission on Centre-State Relations appointed in 2007?
x: Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi, a former Chief Justice of India, chaired the Commission on Centre-State Relations appointed in 2007.

s: In which year was the Punchhi Commission on Centre-State Relations set up?
x: The UPA government set it up in April 2007; 2010 is the year of its report.

s: In which year did the Punchhi Commission on Centre-State Relations submit its report?
x: The Commission on Centre-State Relations reported in 2010; it was appointed by the Government of India in 2007.

s: Which post had Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi, Chairman of the Commission on Centre-State Relations, held earlier?
o: Chief Justice of a High Court
x: Justice M.M. Punchhi was a former Chief Justice of India, not a retired High Court judge.

s: The Punchhi Commission was to review Centre-State arrangements in the light of changes since which of the following?
x: Its mandate was to review arrangements in the light of changes since the Sarkaria Commission (1983-88), such as Panchayati Raj, reforms, coalition politics and internal security.

s: Which of the following was a member of the Punchhi Commission?
x: Dr N.R. Madhava Menon was a member along with Dhirendra Singh, Vinod Kumar Duggal and Vijay Shanker; Sarkaria and Rajamannar headed earlier bodies.

s: How many recommendations did the Punchhi Commission make in its report?
x: The Punchhi report (2010) had 7 volumes and 273 recommendations.

s: Which government set up the Rajamannar Committee on Centre-State relations (1969)?
x: Rajamannar is the only one of the three commissions set up by a State – Tamil Nadu; Sarkaria and Punchhi were set up by the Centre.

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Punchhi Commission
2. Rajamannar Committee
3. Sarkaria Commission
x: Rajamannar (1969), Sarkaria (1983), Punchhi (2007).

s:
Consider the following statements about commissions on Centre-State relations:
1. The Sarkaria Commission was set up in 1983 and reported in 1988.
2. The Rajamannar Committee was appointed by the Centre.
3. The Punchhi Commission recommended that the Inter-State Council meet at least thrice a year.
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Rajamannar Committee was appointed by the Tamil Nadu government.

s: Which of the following bodies recommended an Inter-State Council to be consulted on matters of national importance?
x: The Rajamannar Committee (1969), set up by Tamil Nadu, recommended such an Inter-State Council.

s: In how many volumes was the Punchhi Commission's report submitted?
x: The 2010 report ran to 7 volumes with 273 recommendations.

s: What did the Punchhi Commission recommend on Articles 355 and 356?
o: they be retained unamended and used freely
they be amended, with Article 356 used sparingly as a last resort
Article 356 be the normal remedy for State political disputes
x: Punchhi recommended amending Articles 355 and 356 and using Article 356 sparingly, only as a last resort and never in a partisan manner.

s: What would a 'localised emergency' under Articles 355 and 356 allow the Centre to do?
o: take over the whole country indefinitely
take over a district or part of a district for a limited period
permanently suspend local governments in the State
dissolve every State Legislature during public disorder
x: A localised emergency would let the Centre take over a specific troubled area, such as a district, for a limited period instead of the whole State.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Punchhi Commission's view on Articles 355 and 356?
o: Article 356 should be used only as a last resort
There is no need to amend Articles 355 and 356
Article 356 should never be used in a partisan way
A localised emergency may cover a district or part of a district
x: Punchhi recommended amending both Articles 355 and 356; 'no need to amend' is the APPSC 2017 trap.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution do laws made by Parliament for a State during President's Rule continue in force after the Proclamation ends, until changed by the State Legislature?
x: Article 357(2) keeps such laws in force after the Proclamation ceases until a competent Legislature alters, repeals or amends them.

s: In the event of communal violence in a State, how did the Punchhi Commission recommend that the Centre may deploy central forces?
o: only after obtaining prior consent from the State Government
only after the approval of the Inter-State Council
suo motu, without prior State consent, for a short period, with consent obtained afterwards
permanently, without any subsequent consultation with the State
x: The recommendation permitted the Centre to deploy central forces suo motu without the State's prior consent for a short period; the State's consent would be obtained afterwards.

s: Which body first recommended deploying central armed forces in States 'either on their request or otherwise'?
x: The idea came from the 1st ARC; Punchhi later recommended suo motu deployment in communal violence.

s: Which of the following was NOT a financial recommendation of the Punchhi Commission?
o: Time periods of the Finance and Planning Commissions should be synchronised with the Five Year Plans
Backward States should get higher central transfers with an area-specific strategy
Cesses and surcharges should be left unlimited
Cesses and surcharges should be limited
x: Punchhi wanted cesses and surcharges limited, not left unlimited.

s: Which of the following States is specifically included among the southern States whose share was raised under the revised formula of the 16th Finance Commission?
x: The revised formula raised the share of the five southern States, including Andhra Pradesh.

s: Who chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission, whose award covers the period 2026-31?
x: Dr. Arvind Panagariya chaired the 16th Finance Commission (2026-31). N.K. Singh chaired the 15th and Y.V. Reddy the 14th Finance Commission; M.M. Punchhi chaired the 2007 Commission on Centre-State Relations.

s: With which of the following did the Punchhi Commission recommend synchronising the periods of the Finance Commission and the Planning Commission?
x: It wanted the Finance and Planning Commissions to coordinate, with their time periods synchronised with the Five Year Plans.

s: At what level did the 16th Finance Commission keep the States' vertical share of the divisible pool?
x: The 16th Finance Commission (2026-31) kept the vertical share at 41%, which the Centre accepted in Budget 2026-27.

s: Which of the following Finance Commission – Chairman pairs is correctly matched?
x: The 14th FC was chaired by Y.V. Reddy, the 15th by N.K. Singh and the 16th by Arvind Panagariya.

s: What did the 16th Finance Commission recommend on cesses and surcharges?
o: It brought them into the divisible pool
It made no recommendation on them and proposed a 'grand bargain'
It capped them at 10% of gross tax revenue
x: The 16th FC made no recommendation on cesses and surcharges and proposed a 'grand bargain' (para 7.67).

s: About what share of gross tax revenue did the divisible pool form in 2025-26, as stated in the Lok Sabha in February 2026?
x: The Finance Minister said cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool, which is about 81% of gross tax revenue in 2025-26.

s: Which one of the following is correct about judicial rulings on Governors' timelines for Bills?
o: The 8 April 2025 Tamil Nadu case fixed timelines, but the 20 November 2025 Presidential Reference held courts cannot impose fixed timelines or deemed assent.
The 2025 Presidential Reference abolished judicial review of Governors.
The 8 April 2025 Tamil Nadu case let Governors withhold assent indefinitely.
The 2025 Presidential Reference made deemed assent mandatory.
x: The Tamil Nadu case (8 April 2025) fixed timelines, but the Presidential Reference opinion (20 November 2025) held that courts cannot impose fixed timelines or deemed assent.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The 11th Inter-State Council meeting was the first in about a decade
The 11th Inter-State Council meeting (16 July 2016) took up the Punchhi recommendations
Article 156 has been amended to remove the words 'during the pleasure of the President'
In State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to the Governor (2023), the Supreme Court held a Governor cannot keep Bills pending indefinitely
x: Article 156 is unchanged, so Governors still hold office during the pleasure of the President.

s: Which meeting of the Inter-State Council, held on 16 July 2016, took up the Punchhi recommendations?
x: The 11th ISC meeting (16 July 2016), the first in about a decade, took up the Punchhi recommendations.

s:
Consider the following statements about the status of the Punchhi recommendations:
1. Article 156 has been amended to drop the pleasure clause.
2. Governors still act as Chancellors of State universities.
x: Only 2 is correct; Article 156 is unchanged and Governors still hold office during the pleasure of the President.

s: Which judgment of 8 April 2025 laid down fixed timelines for Governors on Bills?
o: State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to the Governor
State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
x: State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu (8 April 2025) fixed timelines; the Presidential Reference opinion (20 Nov 2025) said courts cannot impose them.

s: Who was the first Chairman of the First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966)?
x: The First ARC (1966) was first headed by Morarji Desai and later by K. Hanumanthaiya; Setalvad led its Centre-State study team.

s: Who headed the Committee of Governors set up in 1970 to study the role of Governors?
x: Bhagwan Sahay headed the Committee of Governors (set up 1970, reported 1971). R.S. Sarkaria headed the 1983 Commission on Centre-State relations, M.N. Venkatachaliah the NCRWC (2002), and P.V. Rajamannar the Tamil Nadu committee of 1969.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: It was first chaired by M. Veerappa Moily
V. Ramachandran later became its chairman
x: The Second ARC was constituted in 2005; 1966 is the year of the First ARC.

s: Which State government set up the Kurian Joseph Committee (2025) on Centre-State relations?
x: The three-member Kurian Joseph Committee was appointed by Tamil Nadu, like the Rajamannar Committee of 1969.

s: Which body on Centre-State relations was appointed by a State government in 1969?
x: The Rajamannar Committee (1969) was appointed by Tamil Nadu; Sarkaria and the First ARC were Centre-appointed.

s: In which year did the Committee of Governors headed by Bhagwan Sahay, set up in 1970, submit its report?
x: The Bhagwan Sahay Committee was set up in 1970 and reported in 1971.

s: Who succeeded M. Veerappa Moily as Chairman of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission in 2009?
x: The Second ARC was first chaired by Veerappa Moily; V. Ramachandran took over after Moily left in 2009.

s: Who was the first Chairman of the First Administrative Reforms Commission set up in 1966?
x: The First ARC was first chaired by Morarji Desai and later by K. Hanumanthaiah.

s: Who was the Chairman of the Commission on Centre-State Relations set up by the Centre in 1983?
x: The Sarkaria Commission (1983, report 1988) was headed by Justice R.S. Sarkaria.

s: Who succeeded Morarji Desai as Chairman of the First Administrative Reforms Commission?
x: The First ARC (1966) was first chaired by Morarji Desai and later by K. Hanumanthaiah.

s: In which year did the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution submit its report?
x: The NCRWC was set up in February 2000 and reported in 2002.

s: In which year was the Second Administrative Reforms Commission constituted?
x: The Second ARC was constituted on 31 August 2005; it gave 15 reports in 2006-2009.

s: With which of the following did the Indrajit Gupta Committee deal?
x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with electoral reform and State funding of elections, not Centre-State relations.

s: Which of the following is the odd one out with respect to the subject it dealt with?
x: Sarkaria, Rajamannar and Punchhi dealt with Centre-State relations; Liberhan inquired into the 1992 Babri Masjid demolition.

s: Who chairs the Standing Committee of the Inter-State Council, set up in 1996?
x: The Standing Committee of the ISC is chaired by the Union Home Minister; the Inter-State Council itself is chaired by the PM.

s: In May 2018, the Standing Committee of the Inter-State Council finished discussing all 273 recommendations of which body?
x: It completed discussion of all 273 Punchhi recommendations in May 2018.

s: In which year was the Inter-State Council set up?
x: The Inter-State Council came in 1990, after the Sarkaria Commission (1983-88) and before the Punchhi Commission (2007-10).

s: On whose recommendation was the Inter-State Council set up in 1990 under Article 263?
x: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 on the advice of the Sarkaria Commission.

s: Which body recommended a Code of Ethics, Right to Public Services laws and a Department of E-Governance?
x: The Second ARC recommended these, along with financial autonomy for PRIs and ULBs.

s: Which of the following Second ARC Report – subject pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sixth Report – Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution
Seventh Report – Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution
Fifteenth Report – State and District Administration
x: The Sixth Report dealt with Local Governance; Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution was the Seventh Report.

s: Which judicial body was proposed by the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
x: The Second ARC proposed a National Judicial Council (2007-08); the National Judicial Commission and AIJS were NCRWC proposals.

s: Which report of the Second ARC was 'Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution', dealing with inter-state and regional conflicts?
x: The 7th report covered conflict resolution; the 5th was Public Order, the 6th Local Governance and the 15th State and District Administration.

s: Which report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission dealt with Local Governance?
x: The Second ARC's 6th report was on Local Governance, covering devolution to PRIs and ULBs.

s: Which body's reports are called the 'Bible' of administrative reforms?
x: The 15 reports of the Second ARC (2006-2009) are called the 'Bible' of administrative reforms.

s: Who headed the First ARC's study team on Centre-State relations?
x: M.C. Setalvad headed the study team; Morarji Desai and later K. Hanumanthaiah chaired the ARC itself.

s: What did the First Administrative Reforms Commission ask for in 1969?
o: Abolition of the office of Governor
x: The First ARC was the first to ask for an Inter-State Council under Article 263, with the PM, Central ministers and Chief Ministers.

s: How many recommendations on Centre-State relations did the First ARC make?
x: The First ARC made 22 recommendations on Centre-State relations, on which no action was taken at the time.

s: What did the NCRWC recommend in relation to Article 356?
o: Its use only on a Rajya Sabha resolution
x: The NCRWC sought safeguards against misuse of Article 356 (along with greater fiscal autonomy and a stronger third tier); deletion was Rajamannar's demand.

s: Which commission reviewed the Constitution, including issues related to social justice?
o: National Commission to Review Working of Constitution
x: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (Venkatachaliah, 2000) reviewed the Constitution, including social justice.

s: Which body proposed an All India Judicial Service and a National Judicial Commission?
x: The NCRWC proposed the National Judicial Commission; the Second ARC proposed a National Judicial Council.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Centre-State chapter of the NCRWC:
1. It sought greater fiscal autonomy for States.
2. It sought safeguards against misuse of Article 356.
3. It sought a weaker third tier of local bodies.
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the NCRWC wanted a stronger, not weaker, third tier.

s: Who was the Chairman of the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC)?
x: The NCRWC (2000-02) was chaired by Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah.

s: How did the Bhagwan Sahay Committee of Governors describe the Governor?
o: the Union's political agent in the State
only the State's executive head, with no Union role
the presiding officer of the State Legislature
both the State's constitutional head and a link with the Centre
x: The Committee saw the Governor as both the State's constitutional head and a link with the Centre, keeping watch and reporting to the Centre.

s: According to the Bhagwan Sahay Committee, to whom does the Governor report after keeping watch on the State administration?
x: The Committee saw the Governor as the constitutional head of the State and a link with the Centre, reporting to the Centre.

s: The National Integration Council is chaired by whom?
o: The Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission
The Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities
x: The Prime Minister chairs the National Integration Council, which works to fight communalism, casteism and regionalism.

s: Which event did the Sri Krishna Commission, chaired by B.N. Srikrishna, inquire into?
x: The Sri Krishna Commission inquired into the 1992–93 Mumbai riots.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Liberhan Commission was chaired by M.S. Liberhan.
2. It inquired into the Babri Masjid demolition.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Both are true: Justice M.S. Liberhan chaired the commission on the 1992 Babri Masjid demolition.

s: Before which Parliamentary Standing Committee do Centre-State questions such as police and the Inter-State Council usually go?
x: Centre-State issues like police, education and the Inter-State Council usually go to the Standing Committee on Home Affairs.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Standing Committee on Rural Development's reports on devolution to Panchayats:
1. Panchayats are a State subject.
2. Devolution of functions, finances and functionaries is uniform across States.
x: Only 1 is correct; as Panchayats are a State subject, devolution is left to each State and varies across States.

s: The Kurian Joseph Committee said federalism needs a structural reset comparable in ambition to the economic reforms of which year?
x: It called for a reset comparable to the economic reforms of 1991.

s: What does the description of NITI Aayog's approach as 'marble-cake federalism' mainly refer to?
o: the working together of the Centre and States on a common platform through a bottom-up approach
the complete separation of Union and State functions
the financial control of States by the Union
the replacement of State governments by regional councils
x: NITI Aayog uses the expression “marble-cake federalism” for cooperative federalism, in which the Centre and States work together through a bottom-up approach.

s: Which body first recommended the idea of cooperative federalism, in which the Centre and the States work together on a common platform?
x: The Sarkaria Commission first recommended cooperative federalism (APPSC-G1 2017 key). Rajamannar sought state autonomy, the First ARC dealt with administrative matters, and NITI Aayog (2015) later put cooperative federalism into practice through its bottom-up approach.

s: The GST Council and NITI Aayog's State rankings are usually cited, respectively, as examples of:
x: The GST Council is a model of cooperative federalism, whereas NITI Aayog rankings promote competitive federalism.

s: Competitive federalism refers to competition
o: among States, and between States and the Centre in policy, to attract investment and improve outcomes
only between the two Houses of Parliament over financial legislation
among courts over the interpretation of federal provisions
only among municipalities for constitutional status
x: Competitive federalism involves States competing with one another and with the Centre through policy initiatives to attract investment and improve outcomes.

s: What is a competition among district administrations or other local bodies to improve performance called?
x: Competitive sub-federalism means competition among local bodies. District rankings under the Aspirational Districts Programme provide an example.

s: How is planning meant to proceed under NITI Aayog's approach to cooperative federalism?
o: Allocating plan funds from the Centre to States through a single national Five Year Plan
Leaving all planning to the Union Ministries with States only implementing schemes
Assigning planning exclusively to State Finance Commissions
Formulating credible plans at the village level and aggregating them progressively upwards
x: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up approach in which credible village-level plans are formulated and aggregated at higher levels of government, unlike the top-down Planning Commission model.

s: Who described Indian federalism as 'bargaining federalism'?
x: Morris-Jones used 'bargaining federalism'; Wheare called India quasi-federal and Austin cooperative.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: K.C. Wheare called India quasi-federal; Ivor Jennings spoke of a federation with a centralising tendency.

s: Who described the Indian federation as one with a centralising tendency?
x: Ivor Jennings called India a federation with a strong centralising tendency.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under competitive federalism, States compete with each other and with the Centre to draw investment.
2. NITI Aayog's State rankings push States to improve social and development indicators.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: States compete for investment, and rankings push them to improve indicators linked to SDG targets.

s: Who described Indian federalism as 'cooperative federalism'?
x: Granville Austin called Indian federalism cooperative federalism; Morris-Jones said bargaining, Wheare quasi-federal.

s: A Constitutional Body is one that is:
o: created by an Act of Parliament
created by a State Legislature alone
x: A constitutional body is set up and empowered by the Constitution itself, such as the ECI or the CAG; bodies created by law are statutory.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Planning Commission was a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
The National Development Council was set up by an executive order in 1952.
NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution in 2015.
The Planning Commission was set up by a Cabinet resolution in 1950.
x: The Planning Commission (1950) was created by a Cabinet resolution, so it was extra-constitutional and non-statutory.

s: Which of the following is a statutory body, created by an Act of Parliament?
x: Statutory bodies such as the NHRC, Lokpal and NGT are created by legislation; NITI Aayog and the Planning Commission came by Cabinet resolution and the Election Commission is constitutional.

s: Who is the CEO of NITI Aayog?
o: A Union Cabinet Minister with no fixed tenure
A Secretary-rank officer with a fixed tenure
A part-time member chosen by rotation
x: NITI Aayog's CEO is a Secretary-rank officer with a fixed tenure; the Prime Minister is its Chairperson.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NITI Aayog – Union Cabinet resolution, 1 January 2015
Planning Commission – Union Cabinet resolution, 1 January 2015
x: NITI Aayog was created by a Union Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015; the Planning Commission by a Cabinet resolution in 1950 and the NDC by an executive resolution in 1952.

s: What is the State Support Mission of NITI Aayog meant to help States do?
o: replace their elected local bodies with nominated bodies
obtain constitutional status for their planning departments
receive plan grants directly from NITI Aayog
x: The State Support Mission helps States build State Institutions for Transformation. GRIT in Gujarat and MITRA in Maharashtra are examples.

s: Which matters are the Regional Councils of NITI Aayog mainly constituted to deal with?
o: Allocation of funds to individual districts
Issues affecting more than one State
x: Regional Councils address issues that affect more than one State.

s: Which of the two hubs at the core of NITI Aayog leads the engagement of the States with the Centre?
x: NITI Aayog has two hubs: the Team India Hub, which leads State engagement with the Centre (APPSC-GS 2018), and the Knowledge and Innovation Hub, its think-tank arm. DMEO is the monitoring and evaluation office, and there is no 'Regional Council Hub'; Regional Councils are separate forums for issues spanning States.

s: Which body did NITI Aayog replace?
x: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission; it follows a bottom-up approach and has no power to allocate plan grants.

s: Who became Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog in April 2026?
x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri became Vice-Chairperson in April 2026, after Suman K. Bery.

s:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog:
1. It was set up by a Union Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015.
2. It has the power to allocate plan grants to States.
x: Only 1 is correct; NITI Aayog is advisory and has no power to allocate plan grants.

s: Who is the Chairperson of NITI Aayog?
x: The Prime Minister is the Chairperson of NITI Aayog; it has no full-time Chairman.

s: MITRA, a State Institution for Transformation under NITI Aayog's State Support Mission, belongs to which State?
x: Under the State Support Mission, GRIT is Gujarat's and MITRA is Maharashtra's State Institution for Transformation.

s: Who jointly head the Regional Councils of NITI Aayog?
o: The Prime Minister and the Union Home Minister
A Chief Minister by rotation and a Union Minister
The Vice-Chairperson and the CEO of NITI Aayog
The Governors of the States concerned
x: Regional Councils deal with issues of more than one State and are jointly headed by a CM (by rotation) and a Union Minister.

s: Which office of NITI Aayog does monitoring and evaluation of programmes?
x: DMEO is NITI Aayog's monitoring and evaluation arm; Team India Hub handles State engagement.

s: The Chief Ministers of which Union Territories are members of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
o: Puducherry, Lakshadweep, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry
Delhi, Chandigarh, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
x: The Governing Council includes the Chief Ministers of Union Territories having legislatures: Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry.

s: The role of which body did the Governing Council of NITI Aayog take over?
x: The Governing Council, first constituted in February 2015, took over the NDC's role.

s: When was the 11th meeting of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog, where Swarna Andhra @2047 was presented, held?
x: The 11th meeting was held on 11 June 2026; the Council was first constituted in February 2015 and reconstituted in February 2021.

s: Who convened the 2016 committee of Chief Ministers on digital payments?
x: N. Chandrababu Naidu convened the 2016 digital-payments committee, which was separate from the three 2015 NITI Aayog sub-groups.

s: Which of the following pairs of Chief Ministers' committee and convener is NOT correctly matched?
o: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (2015) – N. Chandrababu Naidu
Rationalisation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes (2015) – Parkash Singh Badal
x: The sub-group on rationalisation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes was convened by Shivraj Singh Chouhan; Badal convened Skill Development.

s: The 2015 sub-group of Chief Ministers classified Centrally Sponsored Schemes into which categories?
o: Core of the core, core and optional
x: The 2015 sub-group divided CSS into core of the core, core and optional schemes.

s: The GST Council is provided for in which Article of the Constitution?
x: Article 279A provides for the GST Council, where the Centre holds one-third and the States two-thirds of the votes.

s: What is the Centre's share of the total votes in the GST Council?
x: The Centre holds one-third and the States together two-thirds of the votes.

s: Which of the following is a criticism of the GST Council model of cooperative federalism?
o: Gave the Centre two-thirds of the votes
Was created by a Cabinet resolution
Is chaired by the Union Home Minister
x: Subsuming local taxes curtailed States' taxing powers, and compensation disputes followed; the Centre has only one-third of the votes.

s: With whom is the proposal for establishing Zonal Councils associated?
x: The proposal for Zonal Councils was made by Jawaharlal Nehru.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation
River boards are set up under the Inter-State Council Order, 1990
All five Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister
Zonal Councils are statutory and advisory bodies
x: River boards are set up under the River Boards Act, 1956.

s: Under which of the following were Zonal Councils set up?
x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, chaired by the Union Home Minister.

s: In which year was the North Eastern Council set up?
x: The North Eastern Council dates from 1971.

s: Who is the Chairman of the Inter-State Council?
x: The Inter-State Council under Article 263 is chaired by the Prime Minister.

s: Who chairs all the five Zonal Councils set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
o: Chief Minister of the host State
x: All five Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister.

s: How many Zonal Councils were set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
x: There are five Zonal Councils - North, South, Central, East and West - all chaired by the Union Home Minister.

s: What is the usual Centre-State funding ratio for core Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
x: The usual ratio is 60:40; for North-Eastern and Himalayan States it is 90:10.

s: Which of the following has been advanced as a criticism of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: They eliminate all State contributions to development programmes
They make State Governments responsible for designing all national schemes
They can squeeze State priorities because programme parameters are decided by the Centre
They prevent the Centre from transferring funds to States
x: A major criticism is that CSS may squeeze State priorities because the Centre determines important programme parameters and States must provide matching contributions.

s: What is the Centre-State funding ratio of core Centrally Sponsored Schemes for North-Eastern and Himalayan States?
x: Core CSS are funded 60:40, but 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State-ranking indices?
o: Swachh Survekshan is released by NITI Aayog
NITI Aayog prepares the Export Preparedness Index with the Institute for Competitiveness
The SDG India Index of NITI Aayog is now localised to districts
Export infrastructure and export performance are pillars of the Export Preparedness Index
x: Swachh Survekshan is released by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, not NITI Aayog.

s: Who publishes the Ease of Doing Business State Business Reform Action Plan?
x: The State Business Reform Action Plan rankings are associated with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

s: By which title is the State Health Index also known?
o: Progressive Health and Human Capital Index
x: NITI Aayog’s State Health Index is titled “Healthy States, Progressive India.”

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: School Education Quality Index — Institute for Competitiveness alone
Swachh Survekshan — Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: The School Education Quality Index is associated with NITI Aayog with MHRD, not with the Institute for Competitiveness alone. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: What were Andhra Pradesh's score and category in the SDG India Index 2023-24?
x: Andhra Pradesh scored 74 out of 100 and was classified as a Frontrunner.

s: Approximately what share of India’s shrimp exports is contributed by Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh contributes approximately 70 percent of India’s shrimp exports, a factor associated with its EPI ranking.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank in BRAP 2019 (Ease of Doing Business)?
x: AP was 1st in BRAP 2019, with Uttar Pradesh 2nd and Telangana 3rd.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's overall rank in the Export Preparedness Index 2022?
x: AP was 8th overall and 5th among coastal States; Tamil Nadu was 1st.

s: With which Ministry did NITI Aayog publish the School Education Quality Index?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: SEQI was published by NITI Aayog with the MHRD; the State Health Index involved MoHFW and the World Bank.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank among larger States in the 4th round of the State Health Index (2019-20)?
x: AP was 4th among larger States, after Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.

s: Who publishes the Swachh Survekshan rankings?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: Swachh Survekshan is by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, not NITI Aayog.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank in NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2023-24?
x: Andhra Pradesh ranked 17th in the Fiscal Health Index 2023-24.

s: Which State won the most National Panchayat Awards 2025, finishing ahead of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Karnataka won 6 awards; Andhra Pradesh won 5, tied with Odisha.

s: In which category was Andhra Pradesh placed in the State Business Reform Action Plan 2020, released in June 2022?
x: In BRAP 2020 AP was one of seven Top Achievers, with Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Punjab, Telangana and Tamil Nadu.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank among coastal States in the Export Preparedness Index 2022?
x: In EPI 2022 (July 2023) AP was 8th overall and 5th among coastal States.

s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh cities was NOT among those certified 'Water Plus' by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs in August 2021?
x: In August 2021 MoHUA certified Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati as Water Plus; AP became the first State with more than one such city.

s: The Aspirational Districts Programme, launched by NITI Aayog in January 2018, covers how many districts?
x: The ADP covers 112 districts.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh district from the original list remains in the Aspirational Districts Programme?
x: YSR Kadapa stays; Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam replaced Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh district ranked 1st in India in the ADP Basic Infrastructure theme (March 2026)?
x: Alluri Sitharama Raju district ranked 1st in the Basic Infrastructure theme.

s: The 29 subjects of the Eleventh Schedule may be entrusted to Panchayats under which Article?
x: Article 243G lets States entrust the 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects to Panchayats; it is only a menu and transfers nothing automatically.

s: Under Part IX of the Constitution, the State Finance Commission and the State Election Commission for Panchayats are provided for, respectively, in:
x: Article 243I provides for the State Finance Commission and Article 243K for the State Election Commission, both mandatory under the 73rd Amendment. The reverse pairing is wrong; 243H (taxing powers) and 243G (powers and functions) deal with other matters; Articles 280 and 324 concern the Union Finance Commission and the Election Commission of India.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: State Finance Commission – constituted by the Governor
Union Finance Commission – constituted by the Governor
x: The State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor under Article 243I; the Union Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article 280.

s: Under Article 243Y, whose finances does the State Finance Commission also review?
x: Article 243I covers panchayat finances; Article 243Y makes the same SFC review municipal finances.

s:
Consider the following statements about the State Finance Commission:
1. It is constituted by the President under Article 280.
2. It advises the Governor on the assignment of State taxes and grants-in-aid to local bodies.
3. The Governor lays its report, with an explanatory memorandum, before the State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The SFC is constituted by the Governor under Article 243I; Article 280 and the President relate to the Union Finance Commission.

s: Who chaired Andhra Pradesh's Fifth State Finance Commission (2025-30)?
x: Prof. S. Rathna Kumari chaired AP's 5th SFC, whose report went to the Governor in December 2024; Prof. G. Nancharaiah chaired the 4th SFC.

s: Which was Andhra Pradesh's first State Finance Commission after bifurcation?
x: The 4th SFC under Prof. G. Nancharaiah (report 30 October 2019) was the first after bifurcation.

s: At what interval does the Governor constitute the State Finance Commission?
x: Under Article 243I the Governor constitutes the SFC every five years.

s: Who constitutes the State Finance Commission under Article 243I?
x: The SFC is constituted by the Governor; the Union Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article 280.

s: Who chaired Andhra Pradesh's Fourth State Finance Commission, the first after bifurcation?
x: The 4th AP SFC was chaired by Prof. G. Nancharaiah and reported on 30 October 2019.

s: Which of the following was recommended by Andhra Pradesh's Fifth State Finance Commission (2025-30)?
o: Extra help to local bodies with low per capita income
Abolition of property tax in Gram Panchayats
Merger of Gram Panchayats with municipalities
Immediate transfer of all 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects
x: The 5th SFC sought extra help for low per capita income local bodies and State matching grants to Central FC grants.

s: Which change is associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission award for 2026–31?
o: GDP criterion added; revenue-deficit grants continued
Tax-effort criterion added; revenue-deficit grants dropped
GDP criterion added; revenue-deficit grants dropped
GDP criterion dropped; revenue-deficit grants doubled
x: The 2026–31 award adds a GDP criterion and drops revenue-deficit grants.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated feature of the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants-in-aid framework?
o: Limitation of grants-in-aid to local bodies and disaster management
An overall grants-in-aid figure of ₹9.47 lakh crore for the specified categories
Continuation of revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants
x: Under the stated Sixteenth Finance Commission framework, revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants were dropped. Grants-in-aid were limited to local bodies and disaster management, with total grants-in-aid of ₹9.47 lakh crore.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the 16th Finance Commission and Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Revenue deficit grants were increased and Andhra Pradesh's devolution share fell to 4.05%
Revenue deficit grants ended, while Andhra Pradesh's devolution share fell to 3%
Revenue deficit grants ended, while Andhra Pradesh's devolution share rose to 4.217%
The 16th Finance Commission restored the distinction between special and general category States
x: The 16th Finance Commission for 2026-31 ended revenue deficit grants, while Andhra Pradesh's devolution share rose to 4.217%, from the earlier 4.05%.

s: In what ratio were Fifteenth Finance Commission grants to rural local bodies (2021-26) split into tied and untied parts?
x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission gave ₹2.36 lakh crore to rural local bodies, tied and untied in a 60:40 ratio.

s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission (2026-31), local body grants of about ₹7.91 lakh crore were recommended. What share of these grants goes to urban local bodies?
