x: The 16th FC raised the urban share of local body grants to 45% (about ₹3.6 lakh crore urban against about ₹4.4 lakh crore rural). 36% was the earlier urban share, 41% is the States' share of the divisible pool, and 60 per cent is not the urban share.

s: How much was the Fourteenth Finance Commission's grant to Panchayats?
x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission gave ₹2,00,292 crore to Panchayats out of a total local-body grant of ₹2,87,436 crore; ₹1.18 lakh crore is a wrong figure for it.

s: What was the basic-to-performance grant ratio for municipalities under the Fourteenth Finance Commission?
x: The 14th FC used 80:20 for municipalities (APPSC GS 2019) and 90:10 for Gram Panchayats.

s: How much are Andhra Pradesh's local-body grants under the Sixteenth Finance Commission (2026-31)?
x: AP gets ₹28,785 crore of local-body grants, of which ₹12,150 crore is tied to holding local polls.

s: Which of the following was a condition for Fifteenth Finance Commission grants to local bodies?
o: Publication of audited accounts and property-tax floor rates
Merger of Gram Panchayats with municipalities
x: 15th FC grants needed audited accounts and notified property-tax floor rates; tied grants were for water and sanitation.

s: Under which Article may Panchayats levy taxes, duties, tolls and fees only when authorised by the State Legislature?
x: Under Article 243H Panchayat taxing power depends on State legislative authorisation; property tax is a major own-source revenue.

s: Union Finance Commission grants to Panchayats rest on which Article of the Constitution?
x: Union Finance Commission grants rest on Article 280; grants from the State Consolidated Fund relate to Article 243H and SFC recommendations.

s: Under the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, what is the surcharge on stamp duty that goes to the local body called?
x: Transfer duty, a surcharge on stamp duty (s. 69), goes to the local body; seigniorage fees on quarried materials go to the GP Fund.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, to which fund do seigniorage fees on materials quarried in a village go?
x: Under the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, seigniorage fees go to the GP Fund, and a GP may add a surcharge on seigniorage (s. 60(4)).

s: What is the major own revenue of panchayats?
x: Property (house) tax is the major own-source revenue of panchayats (APPSC GS 2018), as it is for ULBs.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Panchayat revenue?
o: Panchayats have an independent constitutional taxing power
Assigned taxes are State-levied taxes handed over on SFC advice
Union Finance Commission grants are routed through the States
Own taxes may be levied only if the State Legislature authorises
x: Panchayats have no independent constitutional taxing power; they may levy taxes only when the State Legislature authorises under Article 243H.

s: In which year were Article 280(3)(bb) and (c), on augmenting a State's Consolidated Fund for local bodies, added?
x: Clauses (bb) and (c) of Article 280(3) were added in 1992 by the 73rd and 74th Amendments.

s: Under Article 280(3)(bb), on whose recommendations does the Union Finance Commission suggest measures to augment State funds for panchayats?
x: The Union FC's suggestions under Article 280(3)(bb) for panchayats and (c) for municipalities are based on SFC recommendations.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the taxes that form the divisible pool shared between the Union and the States?
x: Article 270 lists the taxes forming the divisible pool; Article 280 sets up the Finance Commission.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes vertical and horizontal devolution?
o: Vertical devolution is between Union and States; horizontal devolution is among the States
Vertical devolution concerns taxes; horizontal devolution concerns borrowing alone
Vertical devolution is among States; horizontal devolution is between Union and States
Both terms refer only to grants to local bodies
x: Vertical devolution divides the divisible pool between the Union and States, while horizontal devolution distributes the States' share among the States.

s: Why does vertical fiscal imbalance arise in India?
o: Some States have higher per capita income than others
The States have the more buoyant taxes while the Union carries heavier spending duties
The Union has the more buoyant taxes while States carry heavier spending duties
The Union and the States have identical tax bases
x: The Centre controls the more buoyant taxes, while States bear major spending duties such as health, education, agriculture and police.

s: Which one of the following is excluded from the divisible pool of Central taxes?
x: Cesses and surcharges are excluded from the divisible pool. The divisible pool was approximately 81 per cent of gross tax revenue in 2025-26.

s: Who among the following chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
x: Dr Arvind Panagariya chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission. Y.V. Reddy and N.K. Singh chaired the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Finance Commissions respectively.

s: What share of the divisible pool did the Fourteenth Finance Commission recommend for the States?
x: The Fourteenth FC recommended 42 per cent; the Fifteenth and Sixteenth recommended 41 per cent.

s: Why did the Fifteenth Finance Commission cut the States' share of the divisible pool from 42% to 41%?
o: Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory
Cesses were added to the divisible pool
x: The 15th FC reduced the share to 41% because Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory.

s: Who chaired the Fourteenth Finance Commission?
x: Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th FC (constituted 2 January 2013), which raised the States' share to 42%.

s:
Consider the following statements about vertical devolution:
1. The Fourteenth Finance Commission raised the States' share to 42%.
2. The 41% figure of the Fifteenth Finance Commission is the share of local bodies.
3. The Sixteenth Finance Commission retained the States' share at 41%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The 41% figure is the States' share of the divisible pool, not the local bodies' share.

s: What share of the divisible pool did the Thirteenth Finance Commission give to the States?
x: The 13th FC gave 32%; the 14th raised it to 42% and the 15th set 41%.

s: When was the Sixteenth Finance Commission constituted?
x: The 16th FC under Dr Arvind Panagariya was constituted on 31 December 2023; its report was tabled on 1 February 2026.

s: Which new criterion of the 16th Finance Commission, carrying 10% weight, helped Andhra Pradesh's share?
x: The new contribution-to-GDP criterion carried a 10% weight and helped Andhra Pradesh's share by recognising its economic contribution.

s: What weight did the Fourteenth Finance Commission give to income distance?
x: Income distance carried 50 per cent; population 1971 had 17.5, area 15 and forest cover 7.5 per cent.

s: What weight did the Fifteenth Finance Commission give to population (2011) in horizontal devolution?
x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission gave population (2011) a weight of 15 per cent; demographic performance carried 12.5 per cent.

s: Which criterion, weighted 2.5% by the Fifteenth Finance Commission, was dropped by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission dropped the 2.5% tax and fiscal effort criterion and introduced contribution to GDP with 10%.

s: With reference to the horizontal devolution criteria of the Thirteenth Finance Commission, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Thirteenth Finance Commission assigned 47.5 per cent to income distance, termed fiscal capacity distance by that Commission. Population (1971), area and fiscal discipline were assigned 25 per cent, 10 per cent and 17.5 per cent respectively.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes a change introduced by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Demographic performance was measured by total fertility rate alone.
Income distance was calculated from the average of the three largest States.
Forest cover excluded open forests from consideration.
Tax and fiscal effort replaced contribution to GDP.
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission calculated income distance from the average of the top three large States. Its demographic-performance measure was population growth from 1971 to 2011; forest included open forests; and contribution to GDP replaced tax effort.

s: Andhra Pradesh's 'prosperity paradox' in tax devolution arises under which criterion?
x: Income distance gives greater weight to States with lower per capita GSDP, so Andhra Pradesh's above-average per capita income works against it.

s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission assigned the highest weight among the following to which criterion?
x: Income distance received the highest weight under the Fifteenth Finance Commission, at 45 per cent. Demographic performance, forest and ecology, and Population (2011) received 12.5 per cent, 10 per cent and 15 per cent respectively.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's share in tax devolution under the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
x: AP's share rose to 4.217% from 4.05%; all five southern States gained.

s: How is demographic performance measured by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
x: The 16th FC measures demographic performance by population growth 1971-2011; the 15th FC used change in TFR.

s: What weight did the Fifteenth Finance Commission give to demographic performance in horizontal devolution?
x: The 15th FC gave demographic performance a weight of 12.5%.

s: What weight did the Fourteenth Finance Commission give to forest cover in horizontal devolution?
x: The 14th FC gave forest cover 7.5%; the 15th and 16th FCs gave forest and ecology 10%.

s: What weight did the Sixteenth Finance Commission give to income distance in horizontal devolution?
x: Income distance got 42.5% under the 16th FC (45% in the 15th, 50% in the 14th); it is still the highest weight.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the maintenance and audit of Panchayat accounts by State law?
x: Article 243J (243Z for municipalities) lets the State law provide for maintenance and audit of accounts.

s: The Technical Guidance and Support provided by the Comptroller and Auditor General over the audit of local bodies was recommended by which Finance Commission?
x: CAG Technical Guidance and Support over local-body audits was recommended by the Eleventh Finance Commission.

s: Under the AP State Audit Act, 1989, what was the Local Fund Audit Department renamed?
x: The Act renamed the Local Fund Audit Department as the State Audit Department, headed by the Director of State Audit.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, who audits local bodies and may levy a surcharge for losses?
x: The Director of State Audit (Finance Department) audits local bodies and can levy a surcharge for losses under s. 10; the CAG gives only technical guidance.

s: What is the transfer of work to field officers within the bureaucracy, without transfer to elected local bodies, called?
x: Administrative delegation or deconcentration keeps functions within the bureaucracy, whereas democratic decentralisation transfers power to elected local bodies.

s: Which of the following represents the increasing order of depth of decentralisation?
x: The order of increasing depth is deconcentration, delegation and devolution. Devolution transfers the greatest degree of authority to the receiving institution.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 73rd Constitutional Amendment?
o: It made reservation mandatory in Panchayati Raj institutions
It provided for State Finance Commissions
It made the transfer of all 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects mandatory
It provided for a State Election Commission
x: The 73rd Amendment made reservation, the SFC and the SEC mandatory, but the 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects are optional, since Article 243G says 'may'.

s: Who among the following used the term 'democratic decentralisation'?
x: Democratic decentralisation, the move of power to elected local bodies, is Balwant Rai Mehta's term.

s: During which period did the Local Finance Enquiry Committee function?
x: The Local Finance Enquiry Committee (P.K. Wattal) sat in 1949-51; the Taxation Enquiry Commission followed in 1953-54.

s: Who chaired the Rural-Urban Relationship Committee (1963-66)?
x: A.P. Jain chaired the Rural-Urban Relationship Committee of 1963-66; P.K. Wattal is linked with the Local Finance Enquiry Committee.

s: Which body (1953-54) recommended that some taxes be reserved for local bodies?
x: The Taxation Enquiry Commission of 1953-54 recommended reserving some taxes for local bodies.

s: Who headed the Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1949-51)?
x: The Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1949-51) was headed by P.K. Wattal.

s: For what does AMRUT 2.0 specifically reward urban local bodies?
x: AMRUT 2.0 rewards progress in property-tax reform and resource mobilisation through municipal bonds.

s: How does the SVAMITVA scheme mainly strengthen rural local finance?
o: Providing unconditional grants to Gram Panchayats
Transferring urban property taxes to rural bodies
Using drone maps to create a rural property-tax baseline
Issuing municipal bonds for village councils
x: SVAMITVA drone mapping helps create a baseline for rural properties, which can support the development of rural property-tax systems.

s: Of which scheme is the Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program a component?
x: The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program and Training of Trainers on own-source revenue are associated with the revamped RGSA.

s: How much did the bonds issued by the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation in December 2018 raise?
x: GVMC raised ₹80 crore at 10% in December 2018 through BSE-listed municipal bonds.

s: What did the RBI Report on Municipal Finances (November 2024) put municipal corporations' revenue in 2023-24 at?
x: The RBI report put corporations' revenue at 0.6% of GDP, found bonds negligible and urged GIS mapping for property tax.

s: Who publishes the report titled 'Status of Devolution to Panchayats in States'?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, prepared with the National Institute of Urban Affairs
Ministry of Panchayati Raj, prepared with IIPA
Ministry of Rural Development, prepared with NIRDPR
Ministry of Finance, prepared with the Finance Commission
x: The Devolution Index report is published by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and is prepared with the Indian Institute of Public Administration.

s: Which State ranked first overall in the 2024 Devolution Index released in February 2025?
x: Karnataka ranked first, followed by Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 2024 Devolution Index:
1. It is prepared by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj with IIPA.
2. It measures six dimensions, including Capacity Enhancement and Accountability.
3. Andhra Pradesh scored 54.43, in the medium band.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: the Index is by MoPR with IIPA, not NITI Aayog, has six dimensions, and AP scored 54.43.

s: In the 2024 Devolution Index, which State topped the Functionaries dimension?
x: Tamil Nadu topped Functions, Karnataka Finances and Gujarat Functionaries.

s: Which State topped the Functions dimension of the 2024 Devolution Index?
x: Tamil Nadu topped Functions, Karnataka Finances and Gujarat Functionaries in the 2024 Index.

s: Which State topped the Finances dimension of the 2024 Devolution Index?
x: In the 2024 Devolution Index, Tamil Nadu led Functions, Karnataka led Finances and Gujarat led Functionaries.

s: Which programme was merged into the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan?
x: The Backward Regions Grant Fund (BRGF) was merged into RGSA (APPSC-GS 2018). RGSA converges with Mission Antyodaya rather than absorbing it; SVAMITVA and MPLADS are separate schemes.

s: For achieving which goals does the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), begun in 2018-19, mainly strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions?
x: RGSA aims to strengthen PRIs so that they can contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.

s: The funding pattern under RGSA is correctly represented by which one of the following?
o: Centre:State is 40:60, with 90:10 for Union Territories
Centre:State is 75:25, with no separate pattern for Union Territories
Centre:State is 60:40, 90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States, and 100% Central funding for Union Territories
x: The normal Centre-State ratio is 60:40; it is 90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States, while Union Territories receive 100% Central funding.

s: The revamped RGSA is co-terminus with which period?
o: The Fifteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026
The Fourteenth Finance Commission period, from 2015 to 2020
The Sixteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2027
The Fifteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2026
x: The revamped RGSA runs from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2026 and matches the period of the Fifteenth Finance Commission. The 1 April 2021 starting date is incorrect.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes eGramSwaraj?
o: It provides only online auditing of Panchayat accounts.
It executes works recommended under MPLADS.
It combines Panchayat planning, accounting and reporting.
It prepares property records for rural homes.
x: eGramSwaraj integrates Panchayat planning, accounting and reporting. Online auditing is the specific function of AuditOnline, while property records are associated with SVAMITVA.

s: Where is the National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (NIRDPR) located?
x: NIRDPR, the national training body for rural development and Panchayati Raj, is at Hyderabad.

s: Which e-governance tool is used for the online audit of Panchayat accounts?
x: AuditOnline handles online audit; eGramSwaraj is for planning, accounting and reporting.

s: Which agency conducts the drone survey under the SVAMITVA scheme?
x: SVAMITVA drone mapping is done by the Survey of India to give a 'Record of Rights'.

s: On which date was eGramSwaraj launched along with the SVAMITVA scheme?
x: eGramSwaraj was launched with SVAMITVA on 24 April 2020.

s: With which mission does the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan converge?
x: RGSA (2018-19) strengthens PRIs for the SDGs, covers 117 aspirational districts and converges with Mission Antyodaya.

s: Which body recommended the establishment of a Local Body Ombudsman?
o: First Administrative Reforms Commission in its Sixth Report
Second Finance Commission in its Local Finance Report
Second Administrative Reforms Commission in its Sixth Report
x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended a Local Body Ombudsman in its Sixth Report, titled Local Governance, published in 2007.

s: Which State has an Ombudsman for Local Self Government Institutions under a 2001 amendment of its Panchayat Raj Act?
x: Kerala created the Ombudsman for Local Self Government Institutions through the 2001 amendment of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act.

s: With which subject did the V. Ramachandran Expert Committee (2013) of MoPR deal?
o: Panchayats for delivery of public services
x: The 2013 V. Ramachandran Expert Committee dealt with panchayats for delivery of public services; the Ombudsman idea came from the Second ARC.

s: Which of the following pairs correctly states the number of subjects in the Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules, respectively?
x: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects relating to Panchayats, while the Twelfth Schedule contains 18 subjects relating to municipalities.

s: In practice, to whom do the functionaries meant to serve Panchayats mostly report?
x: Functions are devolved on paper and funds come tied to schemes, while staff continue to report to State line departments.

s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a reason for the underperformance of Panchayati Raj Institutions in the government's Roadmap for Panchayati Raj?
o: Weak devolution of the three Fs
x: The Roadmap identifies weak 3F devolution, bureaucratic control, tied funds, dependence on grants and reluctance to tax. Complete financial autonomy is not listed and contradicts the identified constraints.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about constitutional devolution to local bodies?
o: The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules transfer subjects automatically without legislative action
These Articles say the State Legislature 'may' devolve powers and responsibilities
x: The Schedules do not transfer subjects automatically; Articles 243G and 243W use the discretionary 'may'.

s: Which one of the following is the single most important source of own revenue for Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)?
x: Property tax is the main own-source revenue of ULBs, although it remains under-assessed and under-collected.

s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants for 2026-31, to what level did the urban share rise from 36%?
x: The urban share rises to 45%, with grants split 80% basic and 20% performance.

s: What is the own revenue of Urban Local Bodies in India as a share of GDP?
x: ULB own-source revenue is only about 0.3% of GDP, although cities produce about 67% of GDP.

s: Which of the following is NOT a stated condition associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s local-body grants?
o: Timely constitution of State Finance Commissions
Permanent appointment of Special Officers in place of elected bodies
x: The conditions include properly constituted local bodies, published audited accounts and timely State Finance Commissions. Permanent replacement of elected bodies by Special Officers is not a condition.

s: Delayed local-body elections can jeopardise Central grants because the Sixteenth Finance Commission links grants to:
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission links grants with properly constituted local bodies, audited accounts and timely SFCs, so delayed polls put funds at risk.

s: What is a major concern about State Finance Commission reports?
o: Prepared by the Union Finance Commission
x: State Finance Commission reports are often ignored, which weakens fiscal devolution to local bodies.

s: In what ratio are Sixteenth Finance Commission local-body grants divided between basic and performance grants?
x: The 16th FC splits its local-body grants 80% basic and 20% performance.

s: How are Janmabhoomi committees and secretariats criticised in debates on local devolution?
o: Constitutional planning bodies integrating local plans
Parallel bodies weakening the centrality of PRIs
x: The criticism is that PRIs act mainly as implementing agencies, while parallel bodies such as Janmabhoomi committees and secretariats reduce their centrality.

s: Which of the following is a parallel arrangement that bypasses elected local bodies?
x: MPLADS, like DRDAs, user groups and SHGs, bypasses elected local bodies; DPCs and MPCs are constitutional planning bodies.

s: In which year were village and ward secretariats and volunteers introduced in Andhra Pradesh?
x: They were introduced in 2019, after the Janmabhoomi committees of 2014-19; both were criticised as parallel to gram panchayats and wards.

s: Under MPLADS, who executes the works recommended by a Member of Parliament?
x: Under MPLADS the MP only recommends works; the Implementing District Authority executes them, and RTI applies.

s: Which committee made the Collector the chairman of the Zilla Parishad?
x: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee made the Collector the chairman of the Zilla Parishad; later committees split on the Collector's role.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, who runs local bodies whose elected term has lapsed?
x: Special Officers run lapsed local bodies in AP, a form of bureaucratic control.

s: What is the name of the portal used to monitor works under MPLADS?
x: MPLADS works are tracked on the eSAKSHI portal.

s: During which period did Janmabhoomi committees work in Andhra Pradesh as bodies parallel to Gram Panchayats?
x: Janmabhoomi committees (2014-19) and later village/ward secretariats and volunteers (2019) worked parallel to GPs and wards.

s: Which are the constitutional planning bodies meant to integrate plans at the district and metropolitan levels, respectively?
o: DPC under Article 243ZD and MPC under Article 243ZE
MPC under Article 243ZD and DPC under Article 243ZE
DPC under Article 243G and MPC under Article 243W
DPC under Article 280 and MPC under Article 281
x: The District Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZD, while the Metropolitan Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZE.

s: Article 243D sets a constitutional floor for the reservation of seats for women in Panchayats. What share of seats does Andhra Pradesh reserve for women?
x: Article 243D guarantees at least one-third of seats for women, but many States, Andhra Pradesh included, give 50%. One-third is only the constitutional minimum; 40% and 25% are not the AP figure.

s: After 1993, a dissolved local body must be re-elected within how long of its dissolution?
x: Local bodies have a five-year term, and elections are held before expiry or within six months of dissolution under the State Election Commission.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: State Election Commissioner – Removed like a High Court Judge
Chief Election Commissioner – Removed like a High Court Judge
State Election Commissioner – Appointed by the President
Elections to Municipalities – Conducted by the Election Commission of India
x: Under Article 243K the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and removable only like a High Court Judge; the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court Judge.

s: A State Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner of which of the following?
x: Under Articles 243K/243ZA the SEC is removed like a High Court judge; the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge.

s: What happens to proxy behaviour by male relatives when an elected woman Panchayat representative enters her second term?
x: Proxy ('sarpanch pati') behaviour falls markedly, not rises, when the woman representative enters a second term.

s: Which measure is identified as a response to proxy participation by male relatives in women-led Panchayats?
o: Conducting Panchayat meetings without elected representatives
Appointing Special Officers to run Panchayats
Exemplary penalties in proven proxy cases
x: Capacity building of elected women and exemplary penalties in proven proxy cases were identified as responses.

s: What is the aim of the Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan?
o: Strengthening participation of elected women representatives
x: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats strengthen participation of elected women representatives.

s: Who headed the MoPR advisory committee on proxy representation of women (2025), which suggested exemplary penalties?
x: The Sushil Kumar committee (2025) of MoPR recommended exemplary penalties for proven proxy cases.

s: How much reservation for Backward Classes in rural local bodies did the Andhra Pradesh Cabinet decision of 18 August 2026 provide?
x: It provided 34% BC reservation in rural local bodies and 33⅓% in urban local bodies, with direct election of Mayors and chairpersons.

s: Why is Andhra Pradesh's ₹12,150 crore of Sixteenth Finance Commission grants at risk?
x: AP Mandal and Zilla Parishad polls were due by 23 September 2026, and ₹12,150 crore of grants is tied to holding local polls.

s: How much reservation for Backward Classes in urban local bodies did the AP Cabinet decision of 18 August 2026 provide?
x: The decision gave BCs 34% in rural and 33⅓% in urban local bodies, along with direct election of Mayors and chairpersons.

s: What did the Andhra Pradesh Cabinet decide on 18 August 2026 about Mayors and municipal chairpersons?
o: They will be nominated by the Governor
They will be elected by the ward members
They will be replaced by Special Officers
x: On 18 Aug 2026 the AP Cabinet approved direct election of Mayors and chairpersons, along with BC reservation of 34% rural and 33⅓% urban.
